deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page and this one): X is a stratified space or topos, Y ⊂ X is a closed stratum, and V_{Y,X} is the germ of a tubular neighbourhood of Y in X. The deleted neighbourhood V*_{Y,X} is that germ with Y removed. Grothendieck has just said that the classical requirement of 'normal local triviality' should be replaced by a homotopical one, stated as condition (II). Condition (II) says that the composite V*_{Y,X} → V_{Y,X} ≃ Y is a homotopy fibration. Its fibre is V*_{z,Z}: Z is a normal slice to Y at a point z, and V*_{z,Z} is the deleted germ of Z at z, i.e. the link. He proposes taking (II) as the *definition* of homotopical local triviality of Y ↪ X in topos settings, for example schemes with the étale topology.

The page opens by finishing a parenthesis. In the schematic case one must use profinite homotopy types (Artin–Mazur), localized at the set of primes distinct from the residue characteristics involved. Only in that modified setting can finiteness theorems be proved.

Consequences drawn on this page:
- Choose a base point in a connected component of the link V*_{z,Z}. The fibration gives the long exact homotopy sequence (12): …π_i(V*_{z,Z}) → π_i(V*_{Y,X}) → π_i(Y) → π_{i-1}(V*_{z,Z})…
- Its low-degree tail is (13): π_2(Y) → π_1(link) → π_1(V*_{Y,X}) → π_1(Y) → π_0(link) → π_0(V*_{Y,X}) → π_0(Y). The map π_1(V*_{Y,X}) → π_1(Y) is marked as the one entering an earlier formula (10).
- Suppose z does not locally disconnect Z, i.e. the link V*_{z,Z} is connected. Then Y does not locally disconnect X, and π_1(V*_{Y,X}) is an extension of π_1(Y) by a quotient of π_1(V*_{z,Z}). That quotient is the cokernel of the boundary map π_2(Y) → π_1(link).

What this serves: computing the fundamental group of the deleted neighbourhood of a stratum, to be glued (presumably in (10)) into a van Kampen-type description of π_1 of a stratified space or topos. It is the general version of the classical tame situation: for a smooth divisor, the link is a circle, or étale-locally the tame inertia Ẑ^(p')(1), and one recovers the Grothendieck–Murre extension 1 → Ẑ'(1) → π_1^t(V*) → π_1(Y) → 1.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'quotient of π_1(link)' is correct: it is the image of π_1(link), i.e. the cokernel of π_2(Y) → π_1(link).

In the profinite or étale setting, the long exact sequence for a homotopy fibration of pro-spaces needs care (exactness of pro-groups, Mittag-Leffler/finiteness issues). This is presumably why Grothendieck stresses the prime-to-residue-characteristic localization and finiteness. It is left implicit.

ideas.what: Define homotopical local triviality of a stratum Y ⊂ X by requiring the deleted tubular neighbourhood V*_{Y,X} → Y to be a homotopy fibration with fibre the link V*_{z,Z}, and use this as the definition in topos/étale contexts.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links / homotopically stratified spaces (holink fibration condition); étale analogues via deleted tubular neighbourhoods and exit-path/exodromy formalisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Quinn, 'Homotopically stratified sets' (1988); étale side: Fujiwara, Gabber (deleted neighbourhoods), Barwick–Glasman–Haine 'Exodromy' (2018+)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tame topology, stratified structures and tubular neighbourhoods only in general terms; the precise fibration condition as a definition is not stated there, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Long exact homotopy sequence of link → deleted neighbourhood → stratum, and the low-degree consequence: π_1(V*_{Y,X}) is an extension of π_1(Y) by a quotient of π_1(link) when the link is connected.
ideas.modern_name: Fibration long exact sequence; generalization of the tame fundamental group extension for a punctured neighbourhood of a divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical algebraic topology; divisor case: Grothendieck–Murre, LNM 208 (1971)
ideas.where_published: Divisor case: Grothendieck–Murre, 'The tame fundamental group of a formal neighbourhood of a divisor with normal crossings' (LNM 208); SGA1 XIII.

ideas.what: Use of profinite homotopy types localized away from the residue characteristics (Artin–Mazur) as the setting where finiteness theorems for stratified schemes hold.
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA4/SGA5 finiteness theorems; Artin–Mazur LNM 100

missed.claim: Around 1981, Grothendieck proposes to *define* local triviality of a stratification homotopically, by the condition that the deleted neighbourhood fibres over the stratum with fibre the link. This is essentially Quinn's holink condition for homotopically stratified sets (1988), formulated here for toposes and étale schemes as well. The étale/topos version, with profinite types localized at primes away from the residue characteristics, anticipates later work on étale stratified homotopy theory (exodromy).
missed.quote: et c'est cela qui devrait même, dans le contexte topossique (p. ex. celui des schémas avec la top. étale) servir comme de définition de la "locale trivialité homotopique"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor of the homotopical definition of stratified spaces, and an explicit program for an étale analogue (homotopical local triviality of strata in schemes). That analogue was only partially realized later (Barwick–Glasman–Haine, Haine's stratified homotopy theory).

missed.claim: The program to compute π_1 of the deleted neighbourhood of an arbitrary stratum in a scheme, as an extension of π_1(Y) by a quotient of the prime-to-p link group, generalizing Grothendieck–Murre beyond normal crossings. The page sets it up but does not carry it out.
missed.quote: alors π_1(V*_{Y,X}) est une extension de π_1(Y) par un quotient de π_1(V*_{z,Z})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Tame or prime-to-p fundamental groups of punctured neighbourhoods of singular strata remain only partially understood in general.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is routine (a fibration long exact sequence). The notable point is the explicit early (1981+) proposal to take the homotopy-fibration property of the link as the definition of local triviality, including in the étale topos setting. This predates Quinn and anticipates exodromy-style ideas, but it is only sketched.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'V^*_{Z,Z}' should read V^*_{z,Z}: the first subscript is a cursive lowercase z (a point of the normal slice Z), so the fibre is the link of z in Z. Likewise 'Si on sait p.ex. que z ne disconnecte pas Z localement'.
'cf Artin–Mazur' preceded by a struck-out start ('Arti..'); the crossed-out phrase earlier reads roughly 'faut de finitude' → likely intended 'théorèmes de finitude'.
'ce qui ne vient que dans ce contexte' is likely 'ce n'est que dans ce contexte modifié que l'on peut prouver'.
'(sous π_1(V*) → π_1(Y) : qui intervient dans (10))' is an underbrace annotation 'qui intervient dans (10)' under π_1(V*_{Y,X}) → π_1(Y).
'(en connexe, que Y...)' probably 'en conséquence' or 'ou encore'.
In (12) the first term was corrected in the manuscript from a struck 'Z' to z,Z.
